549: There shall be a court to be known as the Municipal Court of the City of Carrollton.
550:
(a) The municipal court shall be presided over by a chief judge and such part-time, full-time, or stand-by judges as shall be provided by ordinance. The method of selection and terms of such judges shall be provided by ordinance.
(b) No person shall be qualified or eligible to serve as a judge on the municipal court unless he shall have attained the age of 21 years and shall be a member of the State Bar of Georgia. All judges shall be appointed by the city council.
(c) Compensation of the judges shall be fixed by ordinance.
(d) Judges may be removed for cause by a vote of three members of the city council.
(e) Before assuming office, each judge shall take an oath, given by the mayor, that he will honestly and faithfully discharge the duties of his office to the best of his ability and without fear, favor, or partiality. The oath shall be entered upon the minutes of the city council journal.
551: The municipal court shall be convened at regular intervals as provided by ordinance.
552:
(a) The municipal court shall try and punish violations of the city Charter, all city ordinances, and such other violations as provided by law.
(b) The municipal court shall have the authority to punish those in its presence for contempt, provided that such punishment shall not exceed a fine of $200.00 or 20 days in jail.
(c) The municipal court may fix punishment for offenses within its jurisdiction not exceeding a fine of $1,000.00 or imprisonment for not more than six months or both such fine and imprisonment or may fix punishment by fine, imprisonment, or alternative sentencing as now or hereafter provided by law.
(d) The municipal court shall have the authority to establish a schedule of fees to defray the cost of operation and shall be entitled to reimbursement of the actual cost of meals, transportation, and caretaking of prisoners bound over to superior courts for violation of state law.
(e) The municipal court shall have authority to establish bail and recognizance to ensure the presence of those charged with violations before the court and shall have discretionary authority to accept cash or personal or real property as surety bond for the appearance of persons charged with violations. Whenever any person shall give bail for his appearance and shall fail to appear at the time fixed for trial, his bond shall be forfeited by the judge presiding at such time and an execution shall be issued thereon by serving the defendant and his sureties with a rule nisi at least two days before a hearing on the rule nisi.
(f) The municipal court shall have the same authority as superior courts to compel the production of evidence in the possession of any party; to enforce obedience to its orders, judgments, and sentences; and to administer such oaths as are necessary.
(g) The municipal court shall have the authority to bind prisoners over to the appropriate court when it appears by probable cause that state law has been violated.
(h) Each judge of the municipal court may compel the presence of all parties necessary to a proper disposal of each case by the issuance of summonses, subpoenas, and warrants which may be served as executed by any officer as authorized by this Charter or by law.
(i) Each judge of the municipal court shall be authorized to issue warrants for the arrest of persons charged with offenses against any ordinance of the city, and each judge of the municipal court shall have the same authority as a magistrate of the state to issue warrants for offenses against state laws committed within the city.
(j) The municipal court is specifically vested with all the jurisdiction and powers throughout the geographic area of this city granted by law to municipal courts and particularly by such laws as authorize the abatement of nuisances and prosecution of traffic violations.
553: The right of certiorari from the decision and judgment of the municipal court shall exist in all criminal cases and ordinance violation cases, and such certiorari shall be obtained under the sanction of a judge of the county superior court, under the laws of the state regulating the granting and issuance of writs of certiorari.
554: With the approval of the city council, the judge shall have full power and authority to make reasonable rules and regulations necessary and proper to secure the efficient and successful administration of the municipal court; provided, however, that the city council may adopt in part or in toto the rules and regulations applicable to superior courts. The rules and regulations made or adopted shall be filed with the city clerk, shall be available for public inspection, and, upon request, shall be furnished to all defendants in municipal court proceedings at least 48 hours prior to such proceedings.

(Code 1975, § 15-2)
608:
The following acts, among others, are declared to be loud, disturbing and unnecessary noises in violation of this article, but such enumeration shall not be deemed to be exclusive, namely:
(1) Horns, signaling devices, etc. The sounding of any horn or signaling device on any vehicle on any street or public place of the city, except as a danger warning; the creation by means of any such signaling device of any unreasonably loud or harsh sound; the sounding of any such device for an unnecessary and unreasonable period of time; the use of any signaling device except one operated by hand or electricity; the use of any horn, whistle or other device operated by engine exhaust; and the use of any such signaling device when traffic is for any reason held up.
(2) Radios, phonographs, etc. The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound in such manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of the neighboring inhabitants or at any time with louder volume than is necessary for convenient hearing for the persons who are in the room, vehicle or chamber in which such machine or device is operated and who are voluntary listeners thereto. The operation of any such set, instrument, phonograph, machine or device in such a manner as to be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the building, structure or vehicle in which it is located shall be prima facie evidence of a violation of this section.
(3) Loudspeakers, amplifiers for advertising. The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, loudspeaker, sound amplifier or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound which is cast upon the public streets for the purpose of commercial advertising or attracting the attention of the public to any building or structure.
(4) Yelling, shouting, etc. Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling or singing on the public streets at any time or place so as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort or repose of persons in any office, or in any dwelling, hotel or other type of residence, or of any persons in the vicinity.
(5) Animals, birds, etc. The keeping of any animal or bird which by causing frequent or long-continued noise shall disturb the comfort or repose of any person in the vicinity.
(6) Steam whistles. The blowing of any locomotive steam whistle or steam whistle attached to any stationary boiler except to give notice of the time to begin or stop work as a warning of fire or danger, or upon request of proper city authorities.
(7) Exhausts. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any steam engine, stationary internal combustion engine, motor boat or motor vehicle except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(8) Defect in vehicle or load. The use of any automobile, motorcycle or vehicle so out of repair, so loaded or in such manner as to create loud and unnecessary grating, grinding, rattling or other noise.
(9) Loading, unloading, opening boxes. The creation of a loud and excessive noise in connection with loading or unloading any vehicle or the opening and destruction of bales, boxes, crates and containers.
(10) Construction or repairing of buildings. The erection (including excavation), demolition, alteration or repair of any building other than between sunrise and sunset (as determined by the United States Naval Observatory) Monday through Saturday and from 12:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, except in case of urgent necessity in the interest of public health and safety, and then only with a permit from the building official, which permit may be granted: (i) for a period not to exceed three days or less while the emergency continues and which permit may be renewed for periods of three days or less while the emergency continues; (ii) if the building official should determine that the public health and safety will not be impaired by the erection, demolition, alteration or repair of any building or the excavation of streets and highways beyond the time periods set forth herein; (iii) if the building official shall further determine that loss or inconvenience would result to any party in interest if such work were to be prohibited; and (iv) upon application being made at the time the permit for the work is awarded or during the progress of the work.
(11) Schools, courts, churches, hospitals. The creation of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church or court while the same are in use, or adjacent to any hospital, which unreasonably interferes with the workings of such institution, or which disturbs or unduly annoys patients in the hospital, provided conspicuous signs are displayed in such streets indicating that the same is a school, hospital or court street.
(12) Hawkers, peddlers. The shouting and crying of peddlers, hawkers and vendors which disturbs the peace and quiet of the neighborhood.
(13) Drums. The use of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention by creation of noise to any performance, show or sale.
(14) Metal rails, pillars and columns, transportation thereof. The transportation of rails, pillars or columns of iron, steel or other material over and along streets and other public places upon carts, drays, cars, trucks or in any other manner so loaded as to cause loud noises or as to disturb the peace and quiet of such streets or other public places.
(15) Pile drivers, hammers, etc. The operation between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. of any pile driver, steam shovel, pneumatic hammer, derrick, steam or electric hoist or other appliance, the use of which is attended by loud or unusual noise.
(16) Blowers. The operation of any noise-creating blower or power fan or any internal combustion engine, the operation of which causes noise due to the explosion of operating gases or fluids, unless the noise from such blower or fan is muffled and such engine is equipped with a muffler device sufficient to deaden such noise.
(Code 1975, § 15-3; Res. No. 04-2020, 3-2-20)

(a) General. If the city fire marshal's inspection of a premises, building, structure, or any building system reveals, in whole or in part, a clear and inimical threat to human life, safety, or health, the city fire marshal shall issue such notices or orders to remove or remedy the conditions as shall be deemed necessary in accordance with this section, and shall refer the premises, building, structure, or building system to the city's building inspector and codes enforcement officer for any repairs, alterations, remodeling, removal or demolition required.
(b) Unsafe conditions. Structures or existing equipment that are or hereafter become unsafe or deficient because of inadequate means of egress or which constitute a fire hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life or the public welfare, or which involve illegal or improper occupancy or inadequate maintenance, shall be deemed an unsafe condition. A vacant structure which is not secured against unauthorized entry shall be deemed unsafe.
(c) Structural hazards. When an apparent structural hazard is caused by the faulty installation, operation or malfunction of any of the items or devices governed by this article, the city fire marshal shall immediately notify the city's building inspector and codes enforcement officer.
(d) Evacuation. The city fire marshal or the fire department official in charge of an incident shall be authorized to order the immediate evacuation of any occupied building deemed unsafe when such building has hazardous conditions that present imminent danger to building occupants. Persons so notified shall immediately leave the structure or premises and shall not enter or re-enter until authorized to do so by the city fire marshal or the fire department official in charge of the incident.
(e) Summary abatement. Where conditions exist that are deemed hazardous to life and property, the city fire marshal or fire department official in charge of the incident is authorized to abate summarily such hazardous conditions that are in violation of this article.
(f) Abatement. The owner, operator or occupant of a building or premises deemed unsafe by the city fire marshal shall abate or cause to be abated or corrected such unsafe conditions either by repair, rehabilitation, demolition or other approved corrective action.

No person shall operate a motorized vehicle, a Class III electric assisted bicycle, an electric-powered personal vehicle, or a stand-up electric scooter in, over, through or upon the Greenbelt Trail or any portion thereof, except when specifically authorized by law or as authorized below:
(1) Motorized wheelchairs; and/or
(2) Class I and Class II electric assisted bicycles, as defined in section 70-70, and:
a. Manufactured after January 1, 2020; and
b. Shall be equipped with a permanently affixed label in a prominent location which identifies such device as a Class I or Class II electric assisted bicycle along with the wattage and top assisted speed capability printed in at least 9-point Arial font.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12; Res. No. 08-2026, 8-3-26)
706:
No person shall ride a horse in, over, through or upon the Greenbelt Trail, except in areas designated for such use, and where permitted, no person shall ride a horse in a reckless manner or in any other manner which endangers other users of the Greenbelt Trail.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12)
707:
No person shall operate a bicycle or an electric assisted bicycle on the Greenbelt Trail in a reckless manner or in any other manner which endangers other users of the Greenbelt Trail.
(1) All person(s) under the age of 16 are required to wear a bicycle helmet as defined in section 70-70 when operating any bicycle on the Greenbelt Trail. The helmet shall be of good fit and fastened securely upon the person's head with the straps of the helmet.
(2) Any person(s) operating a bicycle or other non-motorized vehicle on the Greenbelt Trail shall come to a complete stop prior to entering any roadway, driveway, or crosswalk at every location the Greenbelt Trail intersects a roadway, sidewalk, or driveway.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12; Res. No. 08-2026, 8-3-26)
708:
No person shall bring any animal on the Greenbelt Trail, except when such animal is under the direction and control of its owner and is secured by a leash, chain, or lead of sufficient strength to prevent it from escaping from its owner. As used in this section, the term "animal" shall include any type of animal, including, but not limited to, dogs, cats, and horses.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12)
709:
No person shall climb the exterior of, repel from, or jump from any bridge, trestle, overpass, wall, cliff, embankment, building, or monument which is located on or adjacent to the Greenbelt Trail.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12)
710:
The Greenbelt Trail is open from dawn until dusk each day, and it shall be unlawful for any person to be on the Greenbelt Trail before sunrise or after sunset, unless otherwise and specifically authorized by law.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12)
711:
It shall be unlawful to possess any alcoholic beverages and illegal drugs on the Greenbelt Trail.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12; Res. No. 08-2014, 5-5-14)
Editor's note— Res. No. 08-2014, adopted May 5, 2014, changed the title of § 70-77 from " Alcoholic beverages, drugs, and non-permitted firearms prohibited" to "Alcoholic beverages and drugs prohibited."
712:
It shall be unlawful to vandalize, mutilate, deface, or steal any portion of the Greenbelt Trail or any amenities thereto.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12)
713:
The following penalties shall be imposed upon conviction of sections 70-71 through 70-78 of this article:
(1) First conviction. A minimum mandatory fine of $50.00.
(2) Second conviction. A minimum mandatory fine of $100.00.
(3) Third and subsequent convictions. A minimum mandatory fine of $500.00 per occurrence.
(Res. No. 03-2012, 1-10-12; Res. No. 08-2026, 8-3-26)

720:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Bundled garden trash means garden trash which is gathered into bundles and tied securely so that each bundle does not exceed three feet in length nor weigh in excess of 50 pounds.
Containerized trash means refuse which is placed in disposable containers and including bundled garden trash, each unit of which shall not exceed three feet in length nor weigh in excess of 50 pounds.
Contractor includes every person, and the agents and employees thereof, engaged in construction, electrical, mechanical, air conditioning, heating, plumbing, roofing, demolition, landscaping, masonry, and allied-type work, and shall include nurserymen, and tree trimmers.
Debris includes residue of any nature accumulating from the activities defined in the definition of "contractor."
Disposable trash containers means plastic bags and cardboard, wooden and corrugated boxes which shall be nonreturnable and shall be collected and packed into the truck as is.
Garbage means all vegetable and animal matter, food and other refuse from a kitchen, market, store or elsewhere, including all matters that decay, attract flies or create disagreeable odors.
Health officer means those persons employed by the county health department who are employed to enforce health regulations of the city and county.
Miscellaneous refuse means small items of rubbish and refuse which are incident to the ordinary conduct of the household, not included in the definitions of "garbage," "trash" or "rubbish."
Multiple residential unit means any duplex, apartment or groups of apartments under a single roof and used for dwelling places for more than one family.
Offal means the inedible parts of a butchered animal and waste parts of the animal.
Plastic bags means a polyethylene or other heavy-duty plastic bag meeting the National Sanitation Foundation standard of 1.5 mils and not exceeding a 30-gallon capacity, with securing twist tie. An untied plastic bag shall not be an approved container.
Rubbish means bushes, trees, limbs, boxes, planks, boards, old furniture, scrap iron, tin and all other articles of similar nature and large in size, that are not included in the definitions of "garbage" or "trash."
Single residential unit means any dwelling place occupied by one family.
Trash means ashes, dirt, paper, yard sweepings and all other accumulations of similar nature and small in size that are not included in the definition of garbage.
Wheeled container means an 80-gallon plastic, covered container permanently attached to a wheeled tubular steel cart designed for use by residential units for storage of household garbage.
(Code 1975, § 9-1)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
722:
The city by and through its proper departments shall collect and dispose of all properly placed garbage, trash, and refuse within the city, and no person shall collect and dispose of or transport over the streets of the city any garbage, trash, or refuse without first obtaining a written permit from the city to do so.
(Code 1975, § 9-27)
723:
Construction refuse shall not be collected by the city, but shall be disposed of by persons in charge of the establishment where such refuse or waste material accumulates. The disposal of construction refuse must be in a manner satisfactory to the sanitation superintendent. In addition, rubbish generated by a commercial landscaper, tree removal service, or paid handyman shall be disposed of by the customer and shall not be removed by the city. In the alternative, the city may, at its sole discretion, remove such construction refuse or rubbish and charge the customer at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 below. The movement of rubbish generated by a commercial landscaper, tree removal service, or paid handyman from one address to another in order to circumvent the above prohibition is strictly prohibited and is punishable upon conviction as provided in section 1-11.
(Code 1975, § 9-28; Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
724:
Every person who disposes of any garbage, rubbish, or industrial refuse, whether required to do so by this article or otherwise, shall make such disposal at the city landfill, or other authorized area, as specified by the superintendent of the sanitation department.
(Code 1975, § 9-29)
725:
No person who shall own or occupy a premises within the city shall permit trash, garbage, or refuse to collect or remain on such premises, except during periods between city sanitation department pickups, and no person who shall own or occupy a premises in the city shall permit garbage, trash, or refuse to be scattered from such premises into the public streets or alleys of the city.
(Code 1975, § 9-30)
726:
All garbage shall be free from liquid and shall be placed and kept covered in a wheeled container.
(Code 1975, § 9-31)
727:
Trash shall be placed and kept in a wheeled container, which container shall always be kept covered.
(Code 1975, § 9-32)
728:
With the exception of furniture, brush and yard clippings, tires, and appliances, all trash must be placed in an individual wheeled container provided by the city. Trash in excess of the capacity of wheeled container shall only be collected as containerized trash when placed adjacent to the wheeled container at curbside on regular collection days. Any such excess trash will be charged to the customer at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 below. Also, where customers repeatedly have excess trash, the city may, at its sole discretion, assign additional wheeled containers to the customer and charge the customer at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 below.
(Code 1975, § 9-33; Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
729:
Rubbish shall not be placed or kept in either garbage container nor in trash container or box, but shall be removed or disposed of by the person on whose premises such rubbish accumulates.
(Code 1975, § 9-34)
730:
It shall be the duty of the occupant of any single or multiple residential unit to place the wheeled container, on the assigned collection day, at front curbside location in such a manner as not to obstruct pedestrian passage, except that the sanitation superintendent may require the wheeled container to be placed on any side of a property for the reasons of topography or efficiency.
(Code 1975, § 9-35)
731:
It shall be the duty of the occupant of any single or multiple residential unit to place the wheeled container at his appropriate curbside location at or before 7:00 a.m. or prior to the arrival of the sanitation truck on the regular collection day, such placement shall not be made before 5:00 a.m. on the regular collection day.
(Code 1975, § 9-36)
732:
It shall be the duty of the occupant of any single or multiple residential unit to remove the container from curbside location to storage location, which storage location shall be nearer to the residential unit located on the premises than to any street abutting such premises. Such removal shall be accomplished not later than 7:00 p.m. on the day the contents thereof are emptied and collected.
(Code 1975, § 9-37)
733:
The owner or occupant of every improved premises, within the city, which is furnished a wheeled container by the city, shall be liable for any damage to such container and shall be liable for the expense of repairs which shall be required other than normal wear and tear. Such repair shall be made by the city and billed to the occupant. If for any reason an occupant shall fail to pay such charges, then the owner of such improved premises shall be liable for the payment thereof. The charges shall be the actual cost of labor and material.
(Code 1975, § 9-38)
734:
The owner or occupant of any improved premises within the city who intends to vacate such premises must notify the sanitation department which will pick up the wheeled container and issue a receipt to such owner or occupant.
(Code 1975, § 9-39)
735:
No person shall overhaul, molest or interfere with the contents of any wheeled container or adjacent containerized trash set out for collection for emptying or removal by the city, unless by permission of the general superintendent. No person shall remove from its assigned premises any wheeled container provided by the city.
(Code 1975, § 9-40)
736:
If the amount of garbage in any single or multiple housing premises is accumulated, the city may require additional wheeled containers sufficient to accommodate the same and an additional charge shall be made for each additional container.
(Code 1975, § 9-41)
737:
Any person who is a full-time resident of a residential unit who is disabled to the extent that he is incapable of moving the wheeled container, in the opinion of the city manager and sanitation superintendent, shall not be required to place the wheeled container at curbside. This section shall not apply unless all of the persons in a residential unit are thus disabled.
(Code 1975, § 9-42)
738:
A monthly sanitary and health charge is hereby fixed and assessed against the owner or occupant of all improved premises within the city for which the occupant shall be liable for payment, but if for any reason an occupant of an improved premises shall fail to pay the monthly charge to the city, then the owner of such improved premises shall be liable for the payment thereof. Each individual charge shall entitle the person making the payment to one wheeled container which is not assignable, but the city shall have no obligation to provide individual wheeled containers to commercial properties unless a rear-loader-type truck already services the immediate vicinity.
(Code 1975, § 9-43; Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
739:
The monthly sanitary and health charges provided for in this article within the city shall be as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the city clerk.
(Code 1975, § 9-44)
740:
Each business and commercial premises and multiple family residence within the city shall be assigned a commercial classification by the city based on the average number of cubic yards of garbage, trash, and refuse collected from such premises within the three preceding months.
(Code 1975, § 9-45)
741:
The city will only collect and remove garbage, trash, or refuse from those premises that receive a water bill from the city. Both commercial and residential garbage charges shall be attached to the water bill, and all residential water customers shall pay the residential garbage charges as long as water service is active. In all instances when a residential or commercial premises is occupied by more than one unit and is served by a single water meter, the sanitary charges applicable to the premises at such location shall all be billed to the person in whose name the water meter is registered at the office of the water department, the sanitary charge to be included thereon for each unit on the premises. In all instances when a residential or commercial premises is occupied by more than one unit and each such unit is served by a separate water meter, the sanitary charges applicable to each unit shall be billed separately and at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 above. Upon failure to pay the bill in accordance with other ordinances applicable thereto, the city, by and through its proper officials may proceed to enforce collection of same as provided by ordinance, and in addition to such remedies failure to pay the bill within 30 days from date of issue will constitute adequate cause to have such water service disconnected and discontinued to that premises.
(Code 1975, § 9-47; Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
742:
Charges for repairs to wheeled containers shall be billed and collected with the following billing of sanitary and health charges. Section 78-52 is applicable to wheeled container repair charges.
(Code 1975, § 9-48)
743:
Should any person liable for payment of the fees and charges hereby fixed and imposed fail to pay the same within ten days after having been billed therefor, the city clerk is authorized to issue an execution therefor against such person in the same manner provided in cases of default in payment of bills to the utility commission and shall deliver such execution to the chief of police for levy and sale as provided by law.
(Code 1975, § 9-49)
744:
Any person failing for any reason or refusing to pay the monthly sanitary and health charge provided for in this article, after having been duly billed for same by the city, shall be deemed guilty of a violation of this Code, and all sanitary and health services and water services provided by the city to the premises for which the monthly charges are past due shall be terminated by the city. This shall be in addition to the penalty provided for violation of this Code.
(Code 1975, § 9-50)
745:
Unless the customer has obtained a special permit from the city, the agents or employees of the city shall not move from any premises within the city any rubbish or trash:
(1) Which exceeds 50 pounds in weight in any one unit or piece;
(2) Which exceeds six feet in length; or
(3) Which due to its size or weight cannot be loaded upon the trash trucks of the city by one employee.
In the absence of a special permit, the city may, at its sole discretion, remove such rubbish or trash and charge the customer at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 above. All rubbish or trash shall be kept separate from leaves, brush, and yard clippings, and all leaves, brush, and yard clippings shall be placed in such a way as to be reasonably accessible to the city's mechanical pickup equipment. In addition, leaves, brush, and yard clippings shall be limited to two cubic yards per two-week collection cycle, and the city will charge for any additional amounts at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 above. The amount of any such leaves, brush, and yard clippings shall be estimated by the city employee responsible for collection and, where disputed, shall be determined by the public works director or his designee, whose decision shall be final. The movement of leaves, brush, and yard clippings from one address to another in order to comply with the two cubic yard limit is strictly prohibited and is punishable upon conviction as provided in section 1-11.
(Code 1975, § 9-51; Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
746:
The provisions of section 78-56 notwithstanding, the city will remove one appliance or one unit of furniture per customer per two-week collection cycle, and the removal of any additional appliances or furniture will be charged at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 above. In addition, the removal of any refrigerators, freezers, air conditioners, or other items containing coolants or refrigerants will be charged at the rates set forth in the fee schedule established pursuant to section 78-50 above. The city will not remove any household items where a resident is moving or relocating or has been evicted. The city will not remove any tires from a commercial establishment.
(Res. No. 14-2006, 9-12-06)
750:
Only domestic waste originating/generated within the county will be allowed to be discharged into the receiving facility. The waste characteristics must be in compliance with the city's current sewer use ordinance, set forth in chapter 94, article III.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 3)
751:
The city reserves the right to refuse waste or to limit the amount of waste to be discharged into the receiving facility.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 4)
752:
All acceptable wastes must be discharged at the city's water and sewer maintenance facility, referred to in this article as the "receiving facility," located at 533 Kings Bridge Road, Carrollton, Georgia.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 5)
753:
The city will receive acceptable wastes at the receiving facility during the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (Monday through Friday) only, except holidays.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 6)
754:
The permitted waste hauler shall have its company name legibly displayed on both sides of all waste hauler vehicles that discharge into the city's receiving facility.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 7)
755:
The permitted waste hauler shall manifest the source, volume and type of all wastes to be discharged into the city's receiving facility upon forms provided by the city. These completed manifests shall be submitted by the waste hauler at the receiving facility before unloading the contents of the waste hauler's tanks. The city reserves the right to verify any and all data provided on the waste hauler's manifest forms. The waste hauler must use the waste manifest forms provided by the city to report every load that is pumped and discharged into the receiving facility. Failure to accurately record every load, falsification of data or failure to transmit this manifest form to the receiving facility operator prior to discharge shall constitute revocation of the waste hauler's permit.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 8)
756:
All manifests completed and received from the waste hauler by the city at the receiving facility shall be considered confidential and shall not be made available to the public.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 9)
757:
The receiving facility operator will provide a sample bottle to the hauler when he files his manifest prior to discharging his load. A representative sample of each load will be turned in to the receiving facility operator. In addition, the permitted waste hauler shall without prior notification allow the city to inspect any and all loads coming into the receiving facility prior to the discharge of that load into the facility. The waste hauler may be required to suspend the discharging until given permission to proceed with the discharge. The city reserves the right to refuse permission to discharge any load that is suspect for any reason deemed appropriate by the receiving facility operator.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 10)
758:
A charge shall be made for the privilege of dumping acceptable wastes into the receiving facility. A record shall be maintained of such dumping, and statements shall be rendered to the waste hauler on a monthly basis. Failure on the part of the waste hauler to promptly pay waste dumping fees by the due date on the invoice shall be just cause for revocation of the waste hauler permit.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 11)
759:
Waste haulers with operations located in the city or in the county shall be required to maintain a current and valid business license for the respective locality. In addition, waste haulers who operate pump septic systems in the city or county shall be required to maintain a respective current and valid business license.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 15)
762:
Waste hauler permits shall be issued only to hauler services that maintain a physical residence in the city or the county.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 1)
763:
The permitted waste hauler shall at all times comply with the standards established in the city's current sewer use ordinance, set forth in chapter 94, article III.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 2)
764:
Waste hauler permits shall be issued for a period of one year. Permits must be renewed prior to the expiration date in order for the waste hauler to continue utilization of the receiving facility for waste discharging purposes.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 12)
765:
A fee as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges shall be levied for the issuance of a waste hauler permit. The same fee shall apply for the annual renewal of waste hauler permits.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 13)
766:
The waste hauler shall reapply for reissuance of the waste hauler permit on a form provided by the city at least 60 days prior to the then-existing expiration date.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 14)
767:
(a) The terms and conditions of the waste hauler permit may be subject to modification by the city at any time as limitations or requirements as identified by the city's ordinances or rules and regulations are modified, or as other just cause exists.
(b) The waste hauler permit may also be modified to incorporate special conditions resulting from the issuance of an administrative or consent order.
(c) The terms and conditions of the waste hauler permit may be modified as a result of new regulatory standards promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency or the state department of natural resources, environmental protection division.
(d) Any waste hauler permit modifications which result in a new condition in the waste hauler permit shall include a reasonable time schedule for compliance, if possible.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 16)
768:
Waste hauler discharge permits are issued to a specific waste hauler for that specific operation and are not assignable to any other waste hauler or transferrable to any other location. Change of ownership and/or legal status of a waste hauler shall obligate the purchaser to submit a waste hauler permit application for consideration by the city.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 17)
769:
The permit issued to the waste hauler by the city may be revoked when, after inspection, monitoring or analysis, it is determined that the waste to be discharged into the receiving facility is in violation of federal, state, local or city laws, ordinances or regulations. Additionally, falsification or intentional misrepresentation of data or statements pertaining to the waste hauler permit application, the waste manifest or other required reporting form shall be cause for permit revocation.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 18)
770:
Upon notification of a permit revocation, the permittee shall cease and desist from discharging any waste into the receiving facility until a revised permit has been issued or until the matter has been resolved by appropriate action.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 19)
771:
The issuance of the waste hauler permit does not convey any property rights in either real or personal property or any exclusive privileges.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 20)
772:
A waste hauler permittee is responsible for protecting the receiving facility from any contributing waste discharges which could inhibit, interfere or otherwise be incompatible with the operations and/or maintenance of the treatment facility including the treatment, use and/or disposal of residuals.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 22)
773:
(a) The permitted waste hauler shall be responsible for complying with all provisions established within the waste hauler permit. Any permittee who discharges or causes a discharge which damages or impairs the city's sewage collection or disposal system shall be liable to the city for any expense, loss or damage caused by such discharge, in addition to other charges, fees, fines and action as outlined in the city's sewer use ordinance, set forth in chapter 94, article III.
(b) Additionally, falsification or intentional misrepresentation of data or statements pertaining to the waste hauler permit application, the waste manifests or other required reporting forms shall be considered a permit violation and will be addressed as such under the guidelines for fines and actions as outlined in the city's sewer use ordinance, set forth in chapter 94, article III.
(Ord. of 2-19-96(2), § 23)
775:
The purpose of this section is to regulate the placement of recycle grease bins within the city. The procedures and requirements of this chapter are intended to promote public health, safety, and welfare by regulating recycle grease bins, ensure that recycle grease bins do not pose a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic, ensure that material does not accumulate outside of the recycle grease bins, and establish criteria that avoid attracting vermin, unsightliness, and public health standards.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
776:
In order to maintain recycle grease bins, all currently operational food service establishments owning and/or using recycle grease bins shall be required to register the recycle grease bin with the City of Carrollton within 90 days of the effective date of this article. Any food service establishment coming into existence after the effective date of this article or obtaining a recycle grease been after the effective date of this article shall be required to register the recycle grease bin within 30 days of delivery of the recycle grease bin or at the time of application for a certificate of occupancy, whichever is sooner. The registration shall include the size, color, and location of the recycle grease bin, as well as any identifying marks contained on the exterior of the recycle grease bin. Only bins designed for the exclusive purpose of storing recycle grease shall be approved.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
777:
Existing recycle grease bins shall be limited to one user per recycle grease bin, whose establishment name shall be delineated on the registration. The recycle grease bin shall not be located in the right-of-way, with the exception of food service establishments located in the central business district. Recycle grease bins shall be locked at all times, except when the user is actively dumping grease into the recycle grease bin. Food service establishments that change ownership are permitted to continue use of an existing registered recycle grease bin. New owners are required to update the registration for the existing recycle grease bin within 30 days of use. Any food service establishment that is not operational for more than 60 days is subject to the provisions in section 78-126.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
778:
Any recycle grease bin first used by a food service establishment after the effective date of this article shall be located within the structure of the food service establishment and shall be limited to one user. New recycle grease bins shall be registered in accordance with section 78-124.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
779:
A recycle grease bin that is unused or unregistered for more than 60 days is deemed abandoned and considered a nuisance, subject to the provisions located in chapter 50 of the City of Carrollton Code of Ordinances.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
780:
Recycle grease bins shall be maintained in good condition and appearance with no structural damage, holes, or visible rust, and shall be free of graffiti. All recycle grease bins shall be free of debris, other containers or buckets used to transport recycled grease, and any other items. Recycle grease bins shall be serviced regularly so as to prevent overflow of grease. The owner of the food service establishment using the recycle grease bin shall be responsible for maintaining the area around each recycle grease bin so that it is free of litter, garbage, and any other undesirable material. At his sole discretion, the city manager may require a sanitation bond for recycled grease bins that are not maintained as stated in this article.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)
781:
Violations of this article shall be punished as provided in section 1-11 of chapter 1 of the City of Carrollton Code of Ordinances.
(Res. No. 13-2021, 10-4-21)

(a) Interference. No person shall unreasonably hamper, obstruct or impede, or interfere with any parade or parade assembly or with any person, vehicle or animal participating or used in a parade.
(b) Driving through parades. No driver of any vehicle shall drive between the vehicles or persons comprising a parade when the vehicles or persons are in motion and are conspicuously designated as a parade.

(Ord. of 6-21-93(2), § 1-5)
815:
(a) For the purpose of controlling traffic and pedestrian congestion and of providing for the public health, safety and general welfare, the following regulations shall pertain to all parades conducted within the city:
(1) All parades shall be conducted along the route specified in the parade permit.
(2) Parades shall be conducted between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.
(3) All parade participants shall assemble for the parade at the time and location designated in the parade permit and shall disperse from public property immediately after the conclusion of the parade.
(4) No parade participant shall drink alcoholic beverages or be under the influence of any intoxicating beverages or drugs.
(5) Materials used in the construction of floats in the parade shall be of fire-retardant materials and shall be subject to such requirements concerning fire safety as may be determined by the fire chief.
(6) Once commenced, the parade shall not stop along the parade route, but shall continue to move at a fixed rate of speed, and any willful delay or willful stopping of such parade, except when reasonably required for the safe and orderly conduct of the parade, shall constitute a violation of the permit.
(7) Once commenced, no additional vehicles, individuals, groups or participants shall be permitted to join the parade.
(8) It shall be the responsibility of the person obtaining the parade permit to police the parade route for discarded literature, publications, or other written materials distributed along the parade route by participants of the parade and literature, publications, leaflets or other written material shall be distributed in such a manner as not to unduly delay or hinder the progress of the parade.
(9) Speeches shall be allowed only at a location designated in the parade permit.
(10) In no event shall speeches, rallies, etc., be conducted in the public street, or along the sidewalks of the city.
(11) The permittee shall advise all participants in the parade, either orally or by written notice, of the terms and conditions of the permit prior to the commencement of the parade and shall sign an acknowledgment that the permittee and the parade participants have read, understand and will comply with the regulations specified in this article and the conditions of the permit.
(b) Any other reasonable regulations or restriction deemed necessary by the chief of police for the protection and safety of the parade participants, viewing public, or for the public health, safety and general welfare of the citizens of the city, may be imposed by the chief of police. However, such additional regulations or restrictions shall be specified in writing to the applicant with all reasons therefor clearly enumerated.
(Ord. of 6-21-93(2), § 1-6; Res. No. 08-2014, 5-5-14)
816:

In any event, the fee shall not be less than $10.00 for a professionally organized parade. In addition thereto, the applicant or organizer shall post a bond in an amount set forth in the schedule of fees and charges per 100 participants or any portion thereof reasonably estimated to participate, the excuse of which shall be conditioned upon the reimbursement of the city for the cost of additional police reasonably used during said parade and for clean up during and immediately following the parade. (Ord. of 6-21-93(2), § 1-7)

There shall be exempt from ad valorem taxation, including all such taxes levied for educational purposes and for state purposes, 100 percent of the following types of tangible personal property:

849:
Every person engaging or about to engage in business as an operator of a hotel in this city shall immediately register with the city clerk on a form provided by said official. 850:
(a) Due date of taxes. All amount of such taxes shall be due and payable to the city clerk monthly on or before the twentieth day of every month next succeeding each respective monthly period. The tax shall become delinquent for each monthly period after the twentieth day of each succeeding month during which it remains unpaid.
(b) Penalty and interest for failure to pay tax by due date. An operator who fails to make any return or to pay the amount of tax as prescribed, shall be assessed a specific penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for one month or less; and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional month or fraction thereof in which such failure shall continue; provided, however, that the aggregate penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00, whichever is greater. Delinquent amounts shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, until paid.
(c) Acceptance of delinquent return and remittance without imposing penalty and interest; authority; requirements. If the failure to make any return or to pay the amount of tax by the due date results from providential cause shown to the satisfaction of the governing authority of the city by affidavit attached to the return, and remittance is made within ten days of the due date, such may be accepted exclusive of penalty and interest.
(d) Waiving of penalty and interest; authority. O.C.G.A. § 48-2-41, relating to the authority to waive interest, and § 48-2-43, relating to the authority to waive penalty, shall apply; provided, however, that the governing authority shall stand in lieu of the Georgia Commissioner of Revenue, and the city shall stand in lieu of the state.
(e) Penalty for fraud. In the case of a false or fraudulent return, or of failure to file a return where willful intent exists to defraud the city of any tax due, a penalty of 50 percent shall be assessed.
(f) Return; remittance; time of filing; operators required to file; contents. On or before the twentieth day of the month succeeding each monthly period, a return for the preceding monthly period together with appropriate remittance shall be filed with the city clerk. The return shall report the gross rent, taxable rent, exempt rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the period, and such other information as may be required by the city clerk. However, if the estimated tax liability for any monthly period shall exceed $2,500.00 for an operator who, in the prior fiscal year remitted tax greater than $2,500.00 in any three consecutive months, such operator shall file an estimated return and remit not less than 50 percent of the estimated tax liability for the monthly period by the twentieth day of that same monthly period. The amount of tax so remitted shall be credited against the amount to be due with the regular return for the monthly period to be filed on the twentieth day of the succeeding month.
(g) Extension of time of filing; authority; requirements; remittance; penalty and interest. The governing authority of the city may, for good cause, extend the time for making returns for not longer than 30 days. No extension shall be valid unless granted in writing upon written application of the operator. Such grant may not be applicable for longer period than 12 consecutive months. An operator granted an extension shall remit tax equaling not less than 100 percent of the tax paid for the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year; such remittance to be made on or before the date the tax would otherwise come due without the grant of extension. No penalty or interest shall be charged during the first ten days of the extension period.
(h) Collection fee allowed operators. Operators collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and paying the amount due, if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be three percent of the amount due, but only if the amount due was not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. of 2-7-00)
851:
(a) Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the city clerk is not satisfied with the return or returns of the tax or the amount of the tax required to be paid to the city by any operator, he may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within his possession or that may come into his possession. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for one or more monthly periods.
(b) Penalty and interest for failure to pay tax. Penalty and interest shall be assessed upon the amount of any determination, as provided by section 86-35.
(c) Notice of determination; service of. The city clerk shall give to the operator written notice of his determination. The notice may be served personally or by mail; if by mail, such service shall be addressed to the operator at his address as it appears in the records of the city. Service by mail is complete when delivered by certified mail with a receipt signed by addressee.
(d) Time within which notice of deficiency determination to be mailed. Except in the case of failure to make a return or of fraud, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the twentieth day of the calendar month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.
(Ord. of 2-7-00)
852:
(a) Estimate of gross receipts. If any operator fails to make a return, the city clerk shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the operator, or as the case may be, of the amount of total rentals in this city which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period or periods in respect to which the operator failed to make the return and shall be based upon any information which is or may come into the possession of the city clerk. Written notice shall be given in the manner prescribed in section 86-36(c).
(b) Penalty and interest for failure to pay tax. Penalty and interest shall be assessed upon the amount of any determination, as provided by section 86-35.
(Ord. of 2-7-00)
853:
(a) Action for delinquent tax; time for. At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected becomes due and payable and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected, the city clerk may bring an action in a court of competent jurisdiction in the name of the city to collect the amount delinquent together with penalty, interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(b) Operator selling or quitting business. If any operator liable for any amount under this article sells out his business or quits his business, he shall make a final return and remittance within 15 days after the date of selling or quitting the business.
(c) Duty of successors or assignees of operator to withhold tax from purchase money. If any operator liable for any amount under this article sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold sufficiently from the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces from the city clerk either a receipt reflecting full payment or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(d) Liability for failure to withhold. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold purchase as required, he shall be personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price.
(e) Credit for tax, penalty or interest paid more than once or erroneously or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax, penalty or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the city, it may be offset by the governing authority. If the operator or person determines that he has overpaid or paid more than once, which fact has not been determined by the city clerk, such person shall have three years from the date of payment to file a claim in writing stating the specific ground upon which the claim is founded. The claim shall be audited. If the claim is approved by the governing authority, the excess amount paid to the city may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person by whom it was paid.
(Ord. of 2-7-00)
854:

(a) In order to be designated as an enterprise zone, a nominated area shall meet at least three of the four criteria specified in subsections (b), (c), (d), and (e) of the enabling legislation. Creation of an enterprise zone shall be consistent with the county and the city comprehensive plans, as amended. in determining whether an area suffers from poverty, unemployment, or general distress, the county board of commissioners and the city council shall use data from the most current United States decennial census and from other information published by the Federal Bureau of the Census, the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics and the state department of labor. In determining whether an area suffers from underdevelopment, the county board of commissioners and city council shall use the data specified in subsection (e) of O.C.G.A. § 36-88-6. This data shall be comparable in point or period of time and methodology employed.
(b) Pervasive poverty shall be evidenced by showing that poverty is widespread throughout the nominated area and shall be established by using the following criteria:
(1) The poverty rate shall be determined from the data in table P121 contained in the Census of Population and Housing, 1990: Summary Tape File 3A, on CD-ROM (Georgia), prepared by the U.S. Bureau of Census (1992);
(2) For each census geographic block group within the nominated area, the ratio of income to poverty level for at least 20 percent of the residents shall be less than 1.0;
(3) In at least 50 percent of the census geographic block groups within the nominated area, the ratio of income to poverty level for at least 30 percent of the residents shall be less than 1.0;
(4) Census geographic block groups with no population shall be treated as having a poverty rate which meets the standards of paragraph (2) of this subsection but shall be treated as having a zero poverty rate for the purpose of applying paragraph (3) of this subsection; and
(5) All parcels of a nominated area must abut and may not contain a noncontiguous parcel, unless nonabutting parcel qualifies separately under the criteria set forth under paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subsection.
(c) Unemployment shall be evidenced by the use of data published by the office of labor information systems of the state department of labor indicating that the average rate of unemployment for the nominated area for the preceding calendar year is at least ten percent higher than the state average rate of unemployment or by evidence of adverse economic conditions brought about by significant job dislocation within the nominated area such as the closing of a manufacturing plant or federal facility.
(d) General distress shall be evidenced by adverse conditions within the nominated area other than those of pervasive poverty and unemployment. Examples of such adverse conditions include, but are not limited to, a high incidence of crime, abandoned or dilapidated structures, deteriorated infrastructure, and substantial population decline.
(e) Underdevelopment shall be evidenced by data indicating development activities, or lack thereof, through land disturbance permits, business license fees, building permits, development fees, or other similar data indicating that the level of development in the nominated area is at least 20 percent lower than other development activity within the county and the city.
